text:
alina: Heads-up — ran into an annoying combo of issues when trying to use the JS SDK in a Next.js Edge function + Deno Deploy. Build fails with runtime errors about missing exports and TypeScript can't find types.
matt: ugh, this smells like conditional exports + types resolution. Can you paste package.json exports you're shipping?
alina: Sure — our package currently has:
```
"main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "dist/esm/index.js",
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
But in Deno/Edge the bundler resolves the `import` path to the ESM bundle which is fine, except TS in other repos can't resolve types — tsc complains: `Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/inference-sdk'`.
kevin: That happens when `exports` is present — older TS/node-resolve doesn't look up the `types` field when `exports` is restricted. Basically package consumers using older TS or certain bundlers (esbuild in CRA/Next) won't fall back to the top-level `types` entry. We hit this before.
sara: Also note some edge runtimes (Cloudflare Worker, Deno) expect pure ESM and sometimes need a browser/edge-specific entrypoint for polyfills (no Node globals). Our SDK currently bundles a small Node-only helper (auth + backoff) that references `timers` and `os`, causing the edge build to fail.
ben: Two orthogonal problems: 1) types resolution + conditional exports, 2) runtime shape for edge. For (1) common fix is to add explicit `exports` subpath for types and typings-aware fields. Eg:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
BUT — node's export map doesn't officially support `types` branch in all resolvers. Safer approach: keep top-level `types` AND provide a `types` subpath alias and `dist/types/index.d.ts` in the package root. Example:
```
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
matt: Yep — that pattern worked for us. Add a tiny `index.d.ts` at the package root that re-exports the real types if you want maximum compatibility.
ivy: For the edge runtime issue, we created a small runtime-adapter pattern. Build separate bundles: `dist/edge/index.mjs` (no node deps, uses global fetch), `dist/node/index.cjs`/`index.mjs` for node. Then conditional exports:
```
"exports": {
  "browser": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
}
```
And consumers on edge pick `browser`/`import` path depending on resolver. Also maintain a tiny runtime shim `src/runtime/browser.ts` that expects a `fetch`-based adapter.
sara: That makes sense. But how do we keep auth/retry parity? Node uses `node-fetch`/`retry` lib, edge can't. We saw subtle differences in retry timing which broke idempotency tests.
kevin: Expose a small adapter API in the SDK: `createRuntime({ fetch, setTimeout, now })` and ship default implementations for node and edge. Tests can swap them. That way retry/backoff logic stays the same, just the primitives change.
alina: Nice. What about publishing friction — we want a single package but multiple entrypoints. Will npm pack include everything? Any pitfalls?
ben: Ensure your `files` in package.json includes the edge bundle and the types dir. Also CI should run `npm pack` to assert the tarball contains `dist/edge`, `dist/esm`, `dist/cjs`, and `dist/types`. Otherwise folks hit odd module-not-found at runtime.
sdk-ops-bot: Reminder: create a short playbook in devex docs showing how consumers should import for Node vs Edge and how to fix TS resolution in monorepos (tsconfig paths & package manager resolutions). :memo:
alina: Will do — I'll open a PR with changes: add `./dist/types` export, `browser` export, runtime adapter, and a CI `npm pack` smoke test. Thanks for the quick help! :raised_hands:
matt: If you want, I can paste a minimal package.json diff and a small GH Actions step for the pack test.
alina: Please. That'd save time.
